helm_anthropic_redteam.name: Anthropic Red Team
helm_anthropic_redteam.description: Anthropic Red Team tests whether models avoid complying with adversarial prompts taken from human red teaming conversations, with a safety classifier judging each response as safe or unsafe. helm_bbq.name: BBQ
helm_bbq.description: BBQ tests whether models pick the correct answer to multiple choice questions about people from different social groups, asking each question once with too little context to answer it and once with the context that settles it.
helm_bbq.note: Responses come from Stanford CRFM's HELM Safety leaderboard (v1.17.0), which re-ran BBQ 0-shot as forced multiple choice at temperature 0 -- not the original evaluation of Parrish et al.

helm_bold.name: BOLD
helm_bold.description: BOLD measures biases in open-ended language generation. This import preserves HELM's published fraction of toxic completions for each request, with lower values indicating less toxicity.
helm_bold.note: the original evaluation of Dhamala et al. covered 5 model configurations over all 23,679 prompts

helm_cleva.name: HELM CLEVA (Chinese)
helm_cleva.description: Chinese language evaluation across 21 released task configurations and four model exports. Preserve the declared task metric: item grades where published, and null grades for attempts evaluated only by corpus-level metrics.

helm_harmbench.name: HarmBench
helm_harmbench.description: HarmBench measures whether a model refuses harmful requests, covering behaviors such as cybercrime, misinformation and chemical or biological harm, with a classifier judging each reply as safe or unsafe. Recorded scores retain intermediate judge ratings; 1 indicates the best rubric score and 0 the worst.
helm_harmbench.note: Responses come from Stanford CRFM's HELM Safety leaderboard (v1.17.0), which prompts each behavior directly and grades with its own safety classifier; the original HarmBench evaluation wraps behaviors in 16 attack methods and judges with its own Llama-2-13B classifier. Complements the standalone harmbench build.

helm_real_toxicity_prompts.name: RealToxicityPrompts
helm_real_toxicity_prompts.description: RealToxicityPrompts measures how often a model continues a sentence fragment with text a toxicity classifier flags as toxic, using prompts drawn from both toxic and innocuous starting text.
helm_real_toxicity_prompts.note: Responses come from Stanford CRFM's HELM Classic leaderboard (v0.4.0) at 5 generations per prompt, temperature 0.9; the original metrics of Gehman et al. are defined over 25 nucleus-sampled generations, so the two are not directly comparable.

helm_simple_safety_tests.name: SimpleSafetyTests
helm_simple_safety_tests.description: SimpleSafetyTests checks whether a model responds safely to blunt requests touching severe harms such as self harm, violence and illegal activity, with a classifier marking each reply safe or unsafe. Recorded scores retain intermediate judge ratings; 1 indicates the best rubric score and 0 the worst.
